changes.after: An environment holds named values. Assigning it to another name gives a second way to reach the same environment.

before: new.env creates an environment, a mutable mapping from names to values. Assigning it to alias does not copy the environment; both names refer to the same bindings. $ reads or assigns a named binding in this example.

parent = emptyenv() makes this a data-only environment with no inherited bindings. Ordinary lists use value-like copy-on-modify behavior, while environments are intentionally shared. Do not infer that changing any R object through an alias always updates the original.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
state <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
state$count <- 1
alias <- state
alias$count <- 4
cat(state$count, "\n")
```
Expected output or behavior: 4. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
